title: Past-Due Wellness Memberships: Late Fee, Suspension of Access and Restoration
content:
A Wellness Membership whose dues draft keeps failing becomes past due.

## Rule

A membership whose draft still fails 7 calendar days after the billing day becomes past due and is billed the late fee of the tier once for that period; access and sessions stop while it is past due. It is restored once every past-due charge is paid. The grace is 7 calendar days on every tier.

## Input, judgement, output

| Input | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| The draft for a billing day still fails 7 calendar days after that billing day | the membership becomes past due | the late fee is billed once for that billing period; access and sessions stop |
| The membership is past due and every past-due charge has been paid | the membership is restored | the membership is active again |

## Timeline (hypothetical billing day of the 15th)

- The 15th: billing day; the draft fails.
- The 22nd: 7 calendar days after the billing day. If the draft still fails, the membership becomes past due and the late fee is billed once for that period.
- From then until every past-due charge is paid: access and sessions stop.
- On payment of every past-due charge: the membership is restored to active.

For a billing day of the 1st, the same count reaches the 8th.

## Points of judgement

- The late fee is billed once for each billing period that becomes past due.
- Restoration follows payment of every past-due charge.
